title: Normal sinus rhythm
نظم جيبي طبيعي
objective: Recognise a regular rhythm with a P wave before every QRS and a normal rate.
التعرف على نظم منتظم مع موجة P قبل كل QRS ومعدل طبيعي.
accessibleDescription: A regular rhythm at about 75 beats per minute. Each beat shows a small rounded P wave, a narrow sharp QRS spike, and a broader T wave, in that order, with an even gap between beats.
The interval from one QRS to the next is constant throughout the strip - there is no irregularity.

question.prompt: What does this rhythm strip show?
question.explanation: Every QRS is preceded by a P wave, the rhythm is regular, and the rate (~75/min) is within the normal adult range - this is normal sinus rhythm.

evidenceSources: ERC 2021 adult advanced life support guidelines

title: Sinus bradycardia
بطء النظم الجيبي
objective: Recognise a sinus rhythm that is regular but slower than normal.
التعرف على نظم جيبي منتظم ولكنه أبطأ من الطبيعي.
accessibleDescription: The same P-QRS-T beat shape as a normal strip, but the beats are spaced much further apart - about 45 beats per minute - and still perfectly regular.
Every QRS still has a P wave in front of it; only the rate has changed, not the beat shape or regularity.

question.prompt: What does this rhythm strip show?
question.explanation: The P-QRS-T morphology and regularity are unchanged from a normal strip, but the rate is well below 60/min - this is sinus bradycardia.

evidenceSources: ERC 2021 adult advanced life support guidelines

title: Sinus tachycardia
تسرع النظم الجيبي
objective: Recognise a sinus rhythm that is regular but faster than normal.
التعرف على نظم جيبي منتظم ولكنه أسرع من الطبيعي.
accessibleDescription: The same P-QRS-T beat shape as a normal strip, but the beats are much closer together - about 130 beats per minute - and still perfectly regular.
Every QRS still has a P wave in front of it; only the rate has increased, not the beat shape or regularity.

question.prompt: What does this rhythm strip show?
question.explanation: The P-QRS-T morphology and regularity are unchanged from a normal strip, but the rate is well above 100/min with narrow QRS complexes - this is sinus tachycardia, not a ventricular rhythm.

evidenceSources: ERC 2021 adult advanced life support guidelines

title: Atrial fibrillation
الرجفان الأذيني
objective: Recognise the absence of discrete P waves and an irregularly irregular QRS timing.
التعرف على غياب موجات P المنفصلة وعدم انتظام QRS بشكل غير منتظم.
accessibleDescription: No two gaps between QRS complexes are the same length - the rhythm is irregularly irregular, not just fast or slow.
There is no discrete, consistent P wave before each QRS; the baseline between complexes is fine and fibrillatory rather than a clean flat line.

question.prompt: What does this rhythm strip show?
question.explanation: Narrow QRS complexes with no discrete preceding P waves and an irregularly irregular R-R interval are the hallmark of atrial fibrillation.

evidenceSources: ERC 2021 adult advanced life support guidelines

title: Ventricular tachycardia
تسرع النظم البطيني
objective: Recognise a regular, wide-complex tachycardia with no discrete P waves.
التعرف على تسرع نظم منتظم عريض المركب بدون موجات P منفصلة.
accessibleDescription: Wide, bizarre-looking complexes recur regularly at a fast rate (about 180/min) with no visible P wave before any of them.
Each complex is much broader than the narrow QRS seen in the sinus-rhythm strips, consistent with a ventricular origin.

question.prompt: What does this rhythm strip show?
question.explanation: This teaching strip depicts a regular wide-complex tachycardia consistent with ventricular tachycardia. Other rhythms can also have wide complexes. Assess the patient urgently, including whether a pulse is present, and follow the local response pathway.

evidenceSources: ERC 2021 adult advanced life support guidelines

title: Ventricular fibrillation
الرجفان البطيني
objective: Recognise a chaotic rhythm with no identifiable P, QRS, or T waves.
التعرف على نظم عشوائي بلا موجات P أو QRS أو T يمكن تمييزها.
accessibleDescription: A completely chaotic, irregular oscillation with constantly varying amplitude and no recognisable P wave, QRS complex, or T wave anywhere on the strip.
There is no organised electrical activity to measure a rate from at all.

question.prompt: What does this rhythm strip show?
question.explanation: In this pulseless patient, the chaotic tracing with no organised complexes represents ventricular fibrillation, a shockable arrest rhythm. Activate the arrest response, start CPR and deliver prompt defibrillation according to local protocol.

evidenceSources: ERC 2021 adult advanced life support guidelines

title: Asystole
توقف القلب (آسيستول)
objective: Recognise apparent asystole and prioritise the patient assessment and arrest response.
التعرف على توقف النشاط الكهربائي الظاهر وإعطاء الأولوية لتقييم المريض والاستجابة لتوقف القلب.
accessibleDescription: A flat line for the entire strip, with no P waves, QRS complexes, or T waves at any point.
A flat line can represent asystole or loss of ECG signal. Assess the patient immediately.

question.prompt: What does this rhythm strip show, and what is the essential first nursing action?
options: Possible asystole. Assess the patient immediately and start the arrest response if indicated while the team verifies the ECG signal.
Ventricular fibrillation - defibrillate immediately without checking anything else
A technical artifact that can be safely ignored
Normal sinus rhythm with very low amplitude
question.explanation: A flat line can represent asystole or loss of ECG signal. Assess responsiveness and breathing immediately and check for a definite pulse per local protocol. If cardiac arrest is suspected, activate the response and start CPR without waiting for a lead check. The team can verify the ECG signal in parallel. Confirmed asystole is non-shockable.

evidenceSources: ERC 2021 adult advanced life support guidelines
